newsitem.title: THAILAND: Alphatec CFO resigns, says firm cannot be saved.
newsitem.headline: Alphatec CFO resigns, says firm cannot be saved.

text.p: The Chief Financial Officer at Thailand's troubled Alphatec Electronics Plc resigned on Friday, saying his move was because the company could not be rescued.

Leslie Merszei, one of two executives who told reporters earlier this week a 10 billion baht ($322.6 million) discrepancy had been discovered in the firm's accounts, said factions within the board were not committed to helping save the firm.
"Certain directors do not know the meaning of transparency, openness and responsiveness," Merszei wrote in a resignation letter obtained by Reuters.
"Certain directors who are also large secured creditors have an inherent conflict of interest," it added.
Alphatec is searching for an emergency 100-200 million baht credit line from local banks but has between $400-450 million in foreign loans to repay.
Alphatec's bond trustee Bankers Trust has called a bondholders meeting next week to discuss the firm's failure to pay out on a put option exercised on a $45 million eurobond earlier this month.
The attitude of certain board members made re-establishing the trust with such creditors impossible at this time, Merszei wrote.
"Unfortunately, I have now concluded that with certain members of the board, it will be impossible to save Alphatec," he wrote.
Some board members had placed their own interests above those of shareholders, creditors, employees and customers, he said.

"It takes a team effort which has to be led by the board of directors, not ruined by a faction of the board of directors, whose prior lack of governance over Alphatec Electronics Plc speaks for itself."

On Monday Alphatec, formally one of Thailand's leading electronics companies, said founder and CEO Charn Uswachoke had resigned after an independent financial review of the firm found the firm had overstated profits by around four billion baht for at least the last three years.
A further six billion baht discrepancy had been discovered caused by improper corporate deals, some of which included fictional transactions supported by paperwork, Alphatec said.
Charn and many other directors had been unwittingly caught by a situation that was beyond their control, Merszei said.
